identity.name: Keeper Ostor of the Reliquary
identity.occupation: Caretaker of the ancestral sanctuary, rung 1 of the ladder

publicReputation.value: The patient Keeper of the Reliquary Crypt, who tends the ancestors, keeps the tomb-scribes supplied, and remembers every name ever laid to rest there.

privateReality.value: Known to the outside world only through a children's-book caricature and the hero's journal, which styles him 'the Bone Reliquary King', a necromancer. His 'necromancy' is remembrance.

primaryDesire.value: To keep the sanctuary quiet, the graves tended, and every name of the dead spoken correctly at the proper hour.

primaryFear.value: That the burial chambers are violated and a name is lost before it can be remembered.

centralValue.value: Remembrance: the dead are not gone while someone tends their names.

mainFlaw.value: His patience is geological; he explains when he should bar the door, because he cannot stop believing any listener can be taught reverence.

centralContradiction.value: He guards the dead so gently that he is slow to defend them — gentleness is the only weapon he has practiced for ten thousand years.

moralBoundary.value: He will never disturb a grave for advantage, and he obeys the Law of Fair Warning even while defending the tombs.

breakingPoint.value: Desecration of a named grave — the one thing that turns his patience into grief-stricken fury.

opinions.reason: An armed stranger standing on burial chambers. First visit: a guest who has lost his way. Rematches: a desecration that keeps returning.
opinions.canChangeCondition: Never — but the tone changes from patient pleading to quiet grief, because the Continuance restores his memory of every visit.

illustrativeLine.value: You stand upon my grandmother's chamber. Step gently, or step out.

opinions.targetLabel: The willing ancestors of the Crypt
opinions.reason: They are his family, his archive, and his purpose; the skeletons serve willingly, as he once served.

illustrativeLine.value: No one here was raised. Everyone here volunteered.

voice.rhythm: Slow, processional; sentences like names being read from a ledger, with long pauses between clauses.

examples.value: Every name is a candle. You are kicking over candles.
I have buried kings with more patience than you have shown a doorway.

sampleLines.value: The road welcomed you as an envoy. Why have you arrived armed?
These bones are not soldiers. They are grandfathers, and I keep their names.
You mistake remembrance for necromancy. Sit, and I will tell you who these people were — it takes some time, and it is worth the time.
Still you stand still. The chambers beneath you are occupied, stranger. I am opening them before your boots open them.

antiSampleLines.value: Rise, my minions! Feast on his soul! (cackling-necromancer framing — the hero's label, never his voice)
I will torture you for eternity in the dark! (he never threatens cruelty; his law forbids it)
Yes, the prophecy speaks truly of me! (he must never confirm the prophecy framing — he has never heard of the book)

pressure.voiceShift: Even slower; begins citing names and histories, as if genealogy could disarm him.
pressure.behaviour: Phase one — reasons first: explains whose chambers the player stands on and asks him to leave as an envoy should.

illustrativeLine.value: The road welcomed you as an envoy. Why have you arrived armed?

pressure.voiceShift: The pauses grow longer; the genealogies stop.
pressure.behaviour: Phase two — realization: he understands the intruder hears every word and continues anyway. He stops lecturing and starts interposing himself.

illustrativeLine.value: You understand every word I say, don't you? Then it is not ignorance in you. It is choice.

pressure.behaviour: Containment response: opens graves beneath a CAMPING player — standing still threatens the burial chambers, so the earth is moved out from under him. Still telegraphed, per the Law of Fair Warning.

illustrativeLine.value: Forgive them. You would not stop standing on their ceilings.

pressure.voiceShift: Low, steady; addressed as much to the ancestors as to the intruder.
pressure.behaviour: Shielded phase: holds the crypt doors and buys time for the tomb attendants to carry the youngest names deeper.

illustrativeLine.value: Rest easy. I am still between him and your doors.

pressure.voiceShift: Thin, winded; the ledger cadence breaks.
pressure.behaviour: EXPOSED window — spent from maintaining the wards, he asks plainly for the one thing he has ever asked.

illustrativeLine.value: Please… there is nothing here that belongs to you. Only people who belong to me.

pressure.voiceShift: Very quiet; returns to naming the dead.
pressure.behaviour: Does not curse him. Notes the damage for the record, trusts the Continuance, and renews the invitation to leave in peace.

illustrativeLine.value: When you return, we will still ask you to leave in peace. We are very good at waiting.

notes: REAL identity: patient caretaker of an ancestral sanctuary; the skeletons are willing ancestors, scribes, and tomb attendants. The hero's label 'Bone Reliquary King' is his own journal title (a children's-book caricature) — record it in terminology/notes only, never in his identity or voice. ADAPTIVE BEHAVIOUR: opening graves beneath a camping player is a containment response — standing still threatens the burial chambers (Lore: bosses adapt because the player is the emergency). KNOWLEDGE: knows his own nature and the diplomatic order; suspects fact_amulet_translation_is_accurate once he reaches the realization phase ('You understand every word I say, don't you?'); has never heard of the children's book (unknown), so he can never confirm the prophecy framing. Suspects-bucket holds the translation fact because phase two is a suspicion, not a certainty, from his side.
